Frozen reference models in Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) refer to using an existing AI system as the reference for training a reinforcement learning agent. The reference model is "frozen" or pre-trained on specific tasks and data, allowing the human supervisor to provide feedback that guides the agent's behavior rather than requiring extensive fine-tuning of the entire model. This approach can be faster and more efficient but may not always capture all nuances learned during the initial training phase.

In Reinforcement Learning with Human Feedback (RLHF), a frozen reference model is one that remains unchanged throughout the learning process. It uses data from previous human demonstrations to improve its own policy without being updated or modified by further interactions with new users. This approach helps maintain consistency and ensures fairness across different rounds of training.

The frozen reference serves as a template that guides the learning process but is not updated with new data, allowing it to retain its accuracy based on historical interactions rather than recent improvements.
